sections.title: PC or laptop (Windows or Linux today)
steps: Write the ISO to a USB stick with the button above (8 GB or more; the stick is erased).

If you want to keep Windows: in Windows, open Disk Management, right-click the Windows partition, choose Shrink Volume and free at least 32 GB. Leave the space unallocated. Then turn off BitLocker or note your recovery key.

Plug the stick in, restart, and open the boot menu (usually F12, F11, Esc or F8 while the logo shows; on some machines Del/F2 opens the firmware, where you pick the stick under Boot). If the stick is not offered, turn off Secure Boot in the firmware; UEFI and legacy/BIOS modes both work.

LLM OS starts from the stick and runs its set-up: your language, name and time zone, then six sliders (how much it asks, internet, where it thinks, model size, guidance, screen). Try it as long as you like; nothing is written to the computer yet.

To install, say "install LLM OS alongside Windows" (uses the free space you made) or "erase the whole disk and install LLM OS". It shows a plan with the exact partitions and asks once; then it copies itself (a few minutes) and offers a restart.
After the restart a boot menu lists LLM OS and Windows. Unplug the stick.
sections.note: Minimum 4 GB RAM and 2 cores; 8 GB and 4 cores are comfortable. Wi-Fi is set up during the first run (when the sliders leave the internet on) or by saying "connect to Wi-Fi <name> with password …".

sections.title: Intel Mac (2010 onwards)
steps: Write the ISO to a USB stick with the button above.

To dual boot: in macOS open Disk Utility, select the internal disk, click Partition, add a partition of at least 32 GB and apply; then select that new partition and click – (remove) so the space stays free (unallocated): LLM OS installs into free space, never into an existing partition. On Macs with a T2 chip, also open Startup Security Utility (hold Cmd+R at start, Utilities menu) and allow booting from external media.
Plug the stick in, restart holding Option (⌥), and choose the orange EFI Boot entry.
Try LLM OS from the stick. When ready, say "install LLM OS alongside macOS"; it uses the free space you made, keeps macOS and the EFI partition, and asks once before writing.
Restart holding Option to choose between macOS and LLM OS; LLM OS can also be made the default from its own settings.
sections.note: Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and later) cannot boot this ISO natively; run LLM OS there as a virtual machine with run-llmos.sh (host-GPU mode uses the Mac's GPU).

sections.title: Apple Silicon Mac (M1, M2, M3, M4)
steps: Use the virtual machine: double-click run-llmos.sh in this folder (QEMU via Homebrew). It opens LLM OS in a window and serves the model on the Mac's GPU.
Native booting needs Asahi Linux support for your Mac generation; it is tracked in BUILD.md and not part of this release.
sections.note: The arm64 ISO in this folder boots on arm64 UEFI machines and in UTM/QEMU virtual machines on this Mac.

sections.title: Virtual machine (any platform)
steps: macOS: double-click run-llmos.sh. Linux: qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -m 4096 -smp 4 -cdrom llmos-x86_64.iso (or boot the .qcow2 disk). Windows: VirtualBox or VMware with the ISO as the optical drive, 4 GB RAM, EFI on or off.
The first run is the set-up: three questions and six sliders. Say "install LLM OS" inside the VM to put it on the virtual disk.
